name: SDN Host HTTP Request Node
description: Host http.request connector (typed contracts 1.0). Method "request": each "request" frame is an HttpRequest (HREQ, module-sdk runtime type: METHOD, URL, HEADERS, BODY, TIMEOUT_MS, MAX_BYTES, CONTEXT) and becomes one http.request hostcall, sent as an SDS $PIV invocation (HttpParams aligned record + raw url / headers / body frames). Each answers with one "response" frame, an HttpResponse (HRSP: URL, STATUS, HEADERS, BODY verbatim, the request's CONTEXT, RETRIEVED_MS), in input order. MAX_BYTES is a response budget: the host errors past it, never truncates. A request the host refuses or fails still answers, with STATUS 0 and ERROR saying why. No JSON and no base64. Capability "http" is required on every host.

externalInterfaces.description: Outbound HTTP through the host http.request hostcall (SDS $PIV). Go server host: 100 MiB response ceiling lowered per request by MAX_BYTES (exceeding it is an error, never a truncation), 30 s default timeout, per-destination egress pacing. SDK NodeHost/BrowserHost: fetch-based, origin allowlists enforced by host policy.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (module-sdk runtime type HREQ): URL required; METHOD empty = GET; HEADERS sorted by lower-case NAME; BODY verbatim; TIMEOUT_MS / MAX_BYTES 0 = the host's defaults; CONTEXT (one size-prefixed FlatBuffer of the caller's) is echoed in the response.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP requests. THIS IS A FAN-IN PORT: the compiled flow runtime does not enforce maxStreams or maxBatch when it fills an invocation, so an upstream node that fans out N requests delivers all N here in ONE invocation; every frame is answered, in input order.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (module-sdk runtime type HRSP): URL answered, STATUS (0 when the request failed, ERROR says why), HEADERS sorted by lower-case NAME, BODY verbatim, the request's CONTEXT, RETRIEVED_MS.

outputPorts.description: EXACTLY ONE HttpResponse per request frame, pushed in input order, so response k answers request k. A request that could not be performed still answers, with STATUS 0 and ERROR; a consumer drops it as it would a 500 while the positional slot stays aligned.

methods.description: Performs one outbound HTTP request per input frame through the host http.request hostcall (typed: SDS $PIV) and emits the responses in input order. Fetches within an invocation are sequential; the hostcall is synchronous.

sequentialJustification.detail: Each request frame becomes one http.request hostcall answered on the calling thread; the host runs independent requests in parallel and this module creates no threads.
